# Driveshaft U-joint removal and installation methods

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Park on hard flat surface, jack up rear end, remove straps, push shaft forward, and install new U-joints. [t1844]

## Parts

- [Partial] Red Loctite, thread locker [t1844]
- Spicer 1310 U-joints: Greasable or non-greasable [t1844]

## Tips & gotchas

- For greasable joints, orient the zerk so it doesn't hit the inner shaft portion and allows access for grease. [t1844]
- [Partial] If rusted beyond reason, use a blow torch to melt old grease and pop out the joint. [t1844]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Nicking the output seal when inserting the driveshaft back in [t1844]
- [Partial] Over-tightening the four rear differential bolts [t1844]
